sources.source_name: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completes 3 years of transforming India's infrastructure landscape
sources.notes: Launched 13 Oct 2021; 44 central ministries and 36 States/UTs; more than 1,600 data layers; 200+ big-ticket projects evaluated by the NPG; 533+ projects mapped by States/UTs; extension to social-sector planning.

sources.source_name: PM Gati Shakti: Transforming India's infrastructure and logistics (press note)
sources.notes: 1,614 data layers; 208 big-ticket projects worth ₹15.39 lakh crore assessed; 434 projects under three railway economic corridors evaluated; District Master Plan portal (beta, 28 aspirational districts); ULIP 930+ registered private companies, 95 live applications.

sources.source_name: PM GatiShakti panel evaluates 396 projects worth ₹18.66 lakh crore; 256 sanctioned, 198 under implementation
sources.notes: Secondary report citing a PIB release (PRID 2297818, not independently retrieved): 396 projects / ₹18.66 lakh crore evaluated through the NPG; 256 sanctioned; 198 under implementation; 57 ministries/departments and 36 States/UTs; 1,700+ data layers; logistics/connectivity projects above ₹500 crore must go through the NPG. As-on date not stated.

sources.source_name: Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals (GCTs): Driving India's logistics transformation
sources.notes: GCT Policy introduced by the Ministry of Railways on 15 Dec 2021; 306 GCTs approved, 118 commissioned; ~₹8,600 crore private investment; GCT freight revenue ₹12,608 crore in 2024-25; New Sanjali GCT is the first on private land along the Western DFC. Capacity figure (192 MTPA) is attributed inconsistently within the document, so it is not used.

sources.source_name: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1077 — Bharatmala Pariyojana
sources.notes: CCEA approved Phase-I on 24 Oct 2017. Component lengths: economic corridors ~9,000 km; inter-corridor & feeder ~6,000; national corridors efficiency ~5,000; border & international connectivity ~2,000; coastal & port connectivity ~2,000; expressways ~800; balance NHDP ~10,000. Original completion target 2021-22.

sources.source_name: Public Accounts Committee (2023-24), 144th Report — Implementation of Phase-I of Bharatmala Pariyojana
sources.notes: Examines CAG Report No. 19 of 2023. Component costs (₹5,35,000 crore total). Sanctioned cost of 26,316 km awarded ₹8,46,588 crore (₹32.17 crore/km vs ₹15.37 crore/km approved; 158.24%); 13,499 km completed by 31 Mar 2023; coastal & port connectivity 20.75% awarded / 5.20% completed; none of 35 planned MMLPs developed by Mar 2023; MoRTH revised estimate ₹10.95 lakh crore.

sources.source_name: Over 22,700 km of roads completed under Bharatmala Pariyojana, government tells Parliament
sources.notes: Reports a Rajya Sabha written reply by the MoRTH Minister on 22 Jul 2026: 26,425 km awarded; 22,709 km constructed up to May 2026; new sanctions under Phase-I discontinued since November 2023. Primary Rajya Sabha text not yet retrieved — upgrade when pinned.

sources.source_name: Building Bharat — Powering infrastructure through Make in India
sources.notes: Bharatmala as on 28 Feb 2025: 26,425 km awarded of 34,800 km; 19,826 km constructed; 6,669 km greenfield awarded / 4,610 km completed; expenditure ₹4,92,562 crore. Same source as the SID logistics record.

sources.source_name: Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway to boost connectivity to key industrial, logistics hubs: FM Sitharaman
sources.notes: Greenfield expressway being developed under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I; Karnataka stretch ~71 km in three packages; described as a priority corridor under the Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor; names Hoskote, Malur, Bangarpet, Narasapura and the proposed Dobbaspet MMLP. No construction progress or opening date.

sources.source_name: Sagarmala: Transforming India's maritime landscape
sources.notes: Launched March 2015; five pillars, 24 categories. As of 24 Mar 2026: 845 projects (₹6.06 lakh crore); 315 completed (₹1.57 lakh crore); 210 under implementation; 320 in planning. Major ports FY 2025-26: record 915.17 MT. SDCL restructured as Sagarmala Finance Corporation (June 2025). Sagarmala 2.0 proposed: ₹85,482 crore budgetary support, ₹3.6 lakh crore total investment. Inland waterway cargo 145.5 MT in FY 2024-25.

sources.source_name: How many CEZs are being planned under Sagarmala?
sources.notes: 14 Coastal Economic Zones proposed, covering all maritime States and UTs; perspective plans prepared for all 14. Undated FAQ page — status may be older than the access date.

sources.source_name: Deendayal Port gets green light for ₹132.51 crore ROB project in latest Sagarmala push
sources.notes: Road over bridge at level crossing LC-235, Deendayal Port (Kandla); ₹132.51 crore; funded under the Sagarmala Programme; appraised by MoPSW's Delegated Investment Board. Purpose: ease the rail crossing bottleneck and speed cargo evacuation.
